data.input_summary: Core library for per-project decision tracking with vector search, plus Claude Code integration. Auto-discovers implicit decisions in legacy codebases, stores with file associations in a portable embedded DB, and dynamically injects relevant context at edit time via layered MCP + hooks + glob rules.

decisions.choice: Hybrid SQL dump — versioned SQL text dump (.claude/decisions.sql) committed to git, automatically applied to local SQLite + sqlite-vec index on first query or post-checkout hook
decisions.reasoning: User chose hybrid over JSONL. SQL dump preserves relational structure (decisions, file associations, tags, confidence, status) while being text-based and git-diffable. Rebuild step creates the sqlite-vec vector index locally. Avoids binary merge conflicts of direct SQLite commit.

Pure Python, no server, ~15ms/chunk CPU. 256d gives 98.8% of 768d quality with 3x storage reduction. Works on any machine with pip install. Replaces Ollama dependency for this specific use case (decisions are smaller than code chunks).

decisions.choice: Phased: v1 comment/commit extraction (proven, low FP), v2 LLM implicit scan (novel, needs validation)
decisions.reasoning: User chose phased approach. v1 ships the known-good (SATD-style comment/commit extraction) while v2 tackles the research gap (implicit decision detection from code behavior). This lets us ship working auto-discovery fast while building toward the novel capability.

decisions.choice: Three-layer injection: (1) MCP hook-triggered auto-injection as primary path, (2) generated glob rules as static fallback, (3) explicit MCP query as escape hatch
decisions.reasoning: User wanted MCP+hooks but more robust. Three layers cover all scenarios: hook fires automatically when MCP server is running, glob rules work when it's not (new machine), explicit query handles semantic search beyond file-scoped matches. No single point of failure.

decisions.choice: Decisions have status field: active, deprecated, superseded, violated. Superseded decisions link to their replacement.
decisions.reasoning: Gemini identified this as an implied missing requirement. Decisions in software are rarely eternal — without lifecycle status, the AI provides stale context that contradicts modern project standards.

decisions.choice: Every decision has a source field (human, ai-discovered, ai-proposed) and linked file paths + optional commit hashes as evidence
decisions.reasoning: Gemini identified need to distinguish human decisions from AI-inferred patterns. Critical for trust — developers must be able to verify and override AI-proposed decisions.

constraints.value: Python/shell ecosystem — core library must be Python, installable via pip
SQLite3 already in use (epics.db, openmemory.sqlite) — consistent with existing patterns
OpenMemory MCP server exists — new MCP server for decisions must coexist, not replace
Must work on new machine after git clone — no Ollama or external service required for basic operation
Scale to 100k+ LOC — sqlite-vec at 256d handles this in <20ms per query
For developer's own projects first, then other teams — design for single-user first, team use later
No language-specific AST parsing in v1 — file/function level, not expression level
Complements OpenMemory (global), does not replace it — per-project scope only
